title: First-Class Appendices for Print Reports and Zwischenbericht Anhänge
description: Add first-class appendix support to the semio print system (print/tex/): an appendix is a document attached to the main report, behaving like a chapter — numbered A, B, C…, labeled Anhang/Appendix, TOC entry, chip styling, cross-referenceable via \appendixref, listed via \listofappendices. Fix a pre-existing bug where window registers (\listoffigures etc.) render header-only because semio@render@register reads the wrong body macro. Wire the feature into all six print templates (report, paper, flyer n/a, zukunftbau forschungsbericht/zwischenbericht/kompaktbericht). Then apply it to mit-bestand/bericht/zwischenbericht/zwischenbericht.tex: convert 9 Anhang markdown documents from temp/ into 8 LaTeX appendices (A-H), including a 67-project table with per-row avatar images sourced from temp/projekt_bilder/ (downscaled ~600px, copied into zwischenbericht/asset/projekt/). Update body cross-references to use \appendixref. Full plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/print-reports-should-be-joyful-haven.md.
summary:
Put each project's photo and Allgemein table side by side as two windows in one row, per the user's request, using the print system's existing `WindowRow`/`WindowItem`/`WindowArrangement` primitives (semio-window.sty) rather than inventing anything new.

Each of the 67 projects in anhang/projekte.tex now has: `\begin{WindowArrangement}[height=30mm] \begin{WindowRow} \WindowItem[0.3]{\begin{Photo}[title=Bild, image-fit=cover]...\end{Photo}} \WindowItem[0.7]{\begin{Table}[title=Allgemein]...\end{Table}} \end{WindowRow} \end{WindowArrangement}` — the image (wrapped in a numbered `Photo` window instead of a bare `\includegraphics`) and the Allgemein table sit side by side as row one, with the existing `Bauteile` table as the full-width row two beneath.

Hit two real rendering bugs while building this and root-caused both with an isolated tectonic test before touching the real file: (1) `image-fit=cover` without an explicit height rendered the photo duplicated/tiled — turned out to be a symptom of (2), not its own bug; (2) `WindowRow` with one `WindowItem` given an explicit `height=` and the sibling left to auto-size caused the sibling's window to inherit and get clamped to that height too (its content then overflowed past the clamped box since the tcolorbox is `breakable` and doesn't clip). Root cause: `WindowRow` used alone (no enclosing `WindowArrangement`) doesn't establish a clean shared height context — an item's explicit height can leak into a sibling that never asked for one. Fixed by wrapping every row in `WindowArrangement[height=30mm]` and giving *neither* individual window its own `height=`, so both adopt the same explicit height cleanly — the documented, intended way to size a row's siblings consistently. Verified this exact fix (both `image-fit=contain` and `cover`) in the isolated test before rolling it out to all 67 projects via script.

Verified: rebuilt the zwischenbericht clean (zero errors, zero unresolved refs) and confirmed via a rendered page crop that Bild and Allgemein now render side by side at consistent height with no overlap or duplication, each with its own correct chip (e.g. "Foto: P.K.1.a", "Tabelle: P.K.1.b"), and Bauteile follows as the full-width row below.
